cards.design_implication: If investigating viral entry or assembly mechanisms, study designs should not assume S protein conformational changes alone drive membrane curvature, but should instead consider lateral reorganization during the assembly phase.
does_not_establish: Specific experimental conditions used to observe the reorganization.
Quantitative metrics of membrane bending forces.
Causal links between other structural components and membrane bending.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We report that assembled S trimers in lumenal cisternae do not alone induce membrane bending but laterally reorganize on the envelope during virion assembly.
limitations: Does not specify the exact molecular triggers for the lateral reorganization.
cards.statement: Assembled S trimers in lumenal cisternae do not alone induce membrane bending but laterally reorganize on the envelope during virion assembly.

cards.design_implication: Experimental setups aiming to capture vRNP recruitment should include observations of membrane curvature or budding sites, as recruitment appears associated with these geometric features.
does_not_establish: Statistical significance of the accumulation at curved membranes.
Specific instrument settings for detecting vRNPs.
Whether this mechanism applies universally to all coronaviruses.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The viral ribonucleoprotein complexes (vRNPs) are accumulated at the curved membrane characteristic for budding sites suggesting that vRNP recruitment is enhanced by membrane curvature.
limitations: The statement of enhancement is described as a suggestion in the source text.
cards.statement: Viral ribonucleoprotein complexes (vRNPs) are accumulated at curved membranes characteristic of budding sites, suggesting membrane curvature enhances vRNP recruitment.

cards.design_implication: Models of SARS-CoV-2 genome packaging should consider multiple discrete vRNP units rather than a single continuous complex to account for the large genome size and spatial constraints.
does_not_establish: Exact count of vRNP complexes per virion.
Detailed structural parameters of the cylindrical assemblies.
Experimental validation of the 'steric flexibility' claim beyond the proposal.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We propose that the genome is packaged around multiple separate vRNP complexes, thereby allowing incorporation of the unusually large coronavirus genome into the virion while maintaining high steric flexibility between the vRNPs.
limitations: This is stated as a proposal in the text.
cards.statement: The SARS-CoV-2 genome is proposed to be packaged around multiple separate cylindrical vRNP complexes, allowing incorporation of the large genome while maintaining steric flexibility.
